key_insight: A calibrated fluid-structure interaction model can accurately reproduce TAVR valve pressure, flow, and leaflet motion across multiple heart rates without recalibrating the boundary parameters.
engineering_relevance: This provides a transferable bench-validation framework for assessing transcatheter aortic valve performance under realistic, measurement-informed forcing conditions.
method: Calibrated reduced-order boundary-model parameters using experimental data at 70 bpm only.
Compared simulation vs. pulse-duplicator measurements at 60, 70, and 80 bpm for pressure, flow, PDVA, and leaflet kinematics.
Held parameters fixed and used measured upstream pressure/flow to construct condition-specific pump-pressure waveforms for validation.
evidence_signal: Normalized RMSE stayed low across conditions: 2.88–3.08% for flow, 7.64–8.07% for upstream pressure, 3.50–6.21% for downstream pressure, and 3.07–4.70% for PDVA.
watch_item: Validation is conditional on measurement-informed upstream forcing, so transferability may be less certain under less controlled or more patient-specific boundary conditions.
paper_title: Experimental Bench Validation of a Computational Fluid-Structure Interaction Model of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Dynamics
